parole.significato: The spindle-shaped embryo stage of Acanthocephala that burrows into the body cavity of its first intermediate host.
parole.testo: From New Latin acanthus (“spine”) (extracted from taxonomic name Acanthocephala) + -or (condition).

parole.significato: Any grass of the genus Agrostis of bentgrasses.
parole.testo: From New Latin agrōstis, via the genus name taxonomic name Agrostis.

parole.significato: Having a structure containing honeycomb-like cavities.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Latin alveolatus, from alveolus (“cavity”). For the protists, a borrowing of taxonomic name Alveolata.

parole.significato: Any plant of the genus Euphorbia, the spurges.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Latin euphorbia by 1601, reinforced by taxonomic name Euphorbia after 1753. Variant form euforbia is attested in Middle English.
